VBO:0200914.summary: Keen to work with its handler, the Mountain Cur brings strong treeing instincts and persistence to a hunt. It often follows a trail with its head raised, circling an older scent until a fresher trail appears; its voice may range from silent to freely barking. Rural American breeders preserved it for squirrel, raccoon and larger game.
VBO:0200914.shortDescription: A persistent tree dog that tends to hunt with its head raised, circling older scent to find a fresher trail.

sources.title: Mountain Cur — Official UKC Breed Standard
sources.evidence: Characteristics directly describes strong desire to please, fast hard hunting with head in air, open/semi-open/silent track, clear carrying bark, circling and drifting cold track until hot track. History identifies rural origins, OMCBA preservation and squirrel/raccoon/all types of big-game use. Summary calibrates these registry tendencies and omits universal trainability, intelligence ranking and household suitability.
